articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bounded-suboptimal search seeks a solution within a factor $w$ of optimal while reducing search effort. Focal Search (FS) uses heuristic guidance within FOCAL, the frontier nodes eligible under the threshold $w f_{\min}$, but its deterministic policy may leave $f_{\min}$ unchanged for many expansions. articles.summary: Researchers introduce Probabilistic Focal Search (PFS), which mixes heuristic-guided and minimum-f expansions to accelerate bounded-suboptimal search by advancing the lower bound.

articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) benchmarks cognitive generalization, the ability to infer and apply abstract rules from limited examples. articles.title: Understanding LoRA Rank Trade-offs in Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning

articles.title: Finishing the Task Is Not Enough: Evaluating Agent Resilience and Considerate Participation under Accumulating Challenge
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustained deployment of generative AI agents requires more than isolated task success. Agents must remain useful across repeated interactions, changing conditions, and dependencies on people within shared workflows, especially as technical, human, and operational disruptions accumulate over time. articles.summary: A paper proposes operational resilience and considerate participation as complementary ways to evaluate generative AI agents facing accumulating technical, human, and operational disruptions.

articles.title: Towards a Deterministic Math Solver for Clinical Language Models
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are unreliable at arithmetic, which is a problem for clinical calculators where a single numerical error changes the recommendation. The standard response is to hardcode each calculator as a validated function, one at a time. We test an alternative: the model does not calculate. articles.summary: A Program-Solve interface has clinical language models write case-specific Python that a restricted local executor runs as a deterministic solver, evaluated on MedCalc-Bench Verified with 1,100 cases.

articles.title: Studying Without a Syllabus: Task-Agnostic Environment Preprocessing
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Before an LLM agent tackles tasks in a new environment, it can inspect available corpora and tools and construct reusable resources such as indices, scripts, or procedural guidance. Most automated adaptation methods, however, rely on task examples, trajectories, or evaluation feedback to decide what to build. articles.summary: Researchers study whether an LLM agent can study an unfamiliar environment without a syllabus, building reusable resources like indices and scripts without task examples or evaluation feedback.

articles.title: When Validation Stops Learning: Auditing Update Admission for Continual Embodied Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Independent evaluation can reject harmful policy updates yet also prevent useful continual learning. We argue that update admission must be assessed through both error control and retained learning opportunities at a stated interaction budget. articles.summary: A paper argues update admission for continual embodied agents must be assessed through both error control and retained learning opportunities, identifying a failure in range-based confidence gates.

articles.title: Decoupling Readiness from Release for Tail-Aware Scheduling of Agentic LLM Workflows
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic LLM workflows consist of sequences of model turns interleaved with tool interactions, so their end-to-end completion time depends not only on inference speed but also on when ready turns are released. Most runtimes release each turn immediately upon readiness. articles.summary: This paper proposes a tail-risk-aware turn release scheduling method for agentic LLM workflows, arguing that eager release of ready turns under contention accumulates unfinished work and increases tail latency. articles.title: Demystifying the Privacy-Utility Trade-off in LLM Interactions
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models into daily tasks relies on context-rich instructions, inevitably exposing sensitive user information. Current privacy-preserving methods typically employ context-agnostic static rules, causing severe utility degradation. articles.summary: This systematic analysis deconstructs the privacy-utility trade-off in LLM interactions, showing that current context-agnostic static sanitization rules cause severe utility degradation and identifying three underlying mechanisms including Context-Dependent Utility.

articles.title: Defining AI Agents: A Compendium of Criteria, Metrics, and Benchmarks
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.11018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The term agent in artificial intelligence lacks a standard definition, complicating the evaluation, comparison, and reproducibility of AI agent research. We address this ambiguity through a survey organized around five dimensions of agenticness: environmental interaction, learning and adaptation, autonomy, goal-directed behavior, and temporal coherence. articles.summary: This survey tackles the lack of a standard definition of AI agents by organizing agenticness around five dimensions — environmental interaction, learning and adaptation, autonomy, goal-directed behavior, and temporal coherence — and synthesizing the metrics, benchmarks, and evaluation frameworks for each.

articles.title: Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.11060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Persistent memory is entering production-oriented agent platforms to help long-horizon agents accumulate experience across sessions. Yet a post-task curator agent restricted to completed trajectories can preserve errors, overgeneralize partial evidence, or retain stale knowledge. articles.title: MOSAIC: Query-Aware Exploration Policy Adaptation for GraphRAG
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.11065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) can connect evidence distributed across a corpus graph, but most systems use largely shared exploration procedures across queries. articles.title: Benchmark Radar: A Living Database and Search Engine for AI Benchmarks and Evaluation
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.11115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmark researchers and developers of large language models (LLMs) and other AI systems need to find relevant evaluations, locate their benchmark datasets and code, and understand the settings behind reported scores. articles.title: Beyond Right and Wrong: Evaluating Second-order Social Reasoning in Large Language Models

articles.summary: CriticGen is a fine-grained, generation-aware evaluation framework that turns evaluation into actionable control for answer improvement. It generates sample-specific evaluation dimensions and scoring criteria to provide actionable feedback for model improvement.

articles.summary: This paper presents MERIT, a benchmark and harness that measures the marginal utility of long-term memory for tool-using LLM agents under explicit cost accounting. It provides episodic tool-use tasks across three domains to evaluate whether remembered facts change agent behavior.

articles.summary: AutoFyn is an agent harness inspired by Expert Iteration that adapts a frozen model by updating persistent state from verified reward signals rather than model weights. It uses an orchestrator to explore and plan multiple approaches with specialized agents in each round.

articles.title: Compiling VGDL into Causal Models

articles.title: Reasoning-Aware Compression: Identifying and Protecting Vulnerable Reasoning Circuits for Energy-Efficient LLM Deployment

articles.title: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents

articles.summary: Suno releases Studio 2.0 with major upgrades including MIDI support, bringing its AI music generation platform closer to a full digital audio workstation.
